title: Async: queues, logs, pub/sub, outbox, sagas, backpressure
summary: Decoupling in time: when a queue helps and when it hides a problem, queue vs log semantics, partitions and consumer groups, delivery guarantees, the transactional outbox, idempotent consumers, DLQs, pub/sub fan-out, sagas, backpressure and load shedding.

labs.title: Tiny partitioned log with consumer groups and offsets
Transactional outbox relay with idempotent consumer

units.title: Reliable events: outbox, idempotent consumers, DLQs and fan-out

outcomes.text: Decide when a queue helps and when it hides a problem: size a queue by latency budget and capacity, compute backlog and recovery time with Little's law, and recognise a metastable failure.
Choose between a queue and a log for a workload, pick a partition key and count, and state precisely what ordering a partitioned log does and does not give.
Implement a partitioned log with keyed placement, offsets, retention, consumer groups, commits and rebalancing (labs/a6/tinylog).
Explain consumer-group rebalancing, generation fencing, hot partitions and how to commit safely when messages are processed in parallel.
Choose a delivery guarantee (at-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once) from ack and commit timing, and explain what Kafka-style transactions do and do not cover.
Explain the dual-write problem and implement a transactional outbox with a leased, at-least-once relay (labs/a6/outbox).
Design idempotent consumers: dedupe table, offset-in-database, natural idempotence or a downstream idempotency key, and size dedupe retention against replay (labs/a6/outbox).
Handle poison messages: classify failures, bound retries, use DLQs with context, reason about ordering consequences and replay safely.
Design pub/sub fan-out with isolated subscriptions, choose log versus queue-per-subscriber and push versus pull, and evolve event schemas safely.
Design and implement a saga orchestrator: orchestration versus choreography, compensations, pivot and retriable steps, timeouts as unknown outcomes, and isolation countermeasures (labs/a6/saga).
Apply backpressure and load shedding: bound queues by age, size admission limits with Little's law, shed by priority and tenant, and avoid autoscaling past the bottleneck.
Implement bounded queues with block, drop-newest and drop-oldest policies, priority shedding, credit-based flow control and a queueing simulator (labs/a6/backpressure).
